stories.title: Citrix NetScaler: check exposure and investigate compromise

bullets.text: The Canadian Cyber Centre warns of critical vulnerabilities affecting NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway.
bullets.quote: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of critical vulnerabilities affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances.

bullets.text: A remote attacker could execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable appliance without authenticating.
bullets.quote: The vulnerability may allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable NetScaler appliance.

bullets.text: Preserve forensic evidence before rebooting, patching, or rebuilding affected appliances, where feasible.
bullets.quote: Preserve forensic evidence before shutting down, rebooting, patching, rebuilding, or otherwise modifying affected appliances, where feasible.

bullets.text: CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772. That signal applies to those CVEs, not every related issue.
bullets.quote: CISA KEV matched CVEs: CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772

details.text: Tracked as CVE-2026-88771 , this vulnerability is an Improper Input Validation vulnerability (CWE-20) . The vulnerability may allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable NetScaler appliance. Successful exploitation could result in complete compromise of the appliance, unauthorized access to applications and services, credential theft, lateral movement, and further compromise of internal systems. Tracked as CVE-2026-88772 , this vulnerability is a Buffer Overflow vulnerability (CWE-119) . Successful exploitation may allow arbitrary code execution, memory corruption, denial of service conditions, or other unintended behaviour on affected appliances. details.text: Organizations should review the Citrix security bulletin to determine whether their deployments are affected, prioritize remediation of Internet-facing systems, and investigate for signs of compromise, particularly where evidence of suspicious activity predates the release of vendor fixes The Cyber Centre also recommends that organizations: contact Citrix or their authorized support provider as soon as possible to obtain the latest security guidance and patch availability information Preserve forensic evidence before shutting down, rebooting, patching, rebuilding, or otherwise modifying affected appliances, where feasible. Preserve appliance logs, remote syslog records, and NetScaler Console logs. Collect support bundles and other diagnostic information that may assist future investigations. Review running processes and active network connections for suspicious or unexplained activity. Examine startup scripts, scheduled tasks, web application directories, and crash dump locations for unauthorized modifications or indicators of persistence. Preserve suspicious files and configurations before changing or removing them. Correlate findings with firewall, DNS, authentication, endpoint, and other supporting telemetry sources. Investigate unexpected outbound connections, unusual administrative access, and suspicious activity on connected systems. Review the attached list of indicators of compromise and investigate to find matching patterns. Follow Citrix guidance for suspected compromises, including isolation of affected appliances and assessment of credential exposure . Conduct an organization-specific risk assessment based on the criticality of affected NetScaler deployments, any suspicious findings, and the limited information currently available. Where operationally feasible and justified by the organization's risk assessment, consider temporarily disabling or shutting down Internet-facing NetScaler appliances until vendor guidance and security updates become available; organizations should carefully weigh the cybersecurity risks of continued operation against the operational and business impacts of service disruption before taking this action. stories.title: Cisco NGOAM: remote code execution risk on affected Nexus switches

bullets.text: Cisco describes possible unauthenticated code execution or denial of service.
bullets.quote: Multiple vulnerabilities in the Operation, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) feature of Cisco NX-OS Software, known as Next Generation OAM (NGOAM), could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges or cause a denial of service (DoS) condition on an affected device.

bullets.text: Nexus 3000/9000 standalone NX-OS exposure depends on NGOAM and vulnerability-specific conditions.
bullets.quote: These vulnerabilities affect Cisco Nexus 3000 Series Switches and Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches in standalone NX-OS mode if NGOAM is enabled and specific features are configured, as detailed in the following list:

bullets.text: If NGOAM is not required, Cisco says disabling it removes the attack vector.
bullets.quote: If the NGOAM feature is not required, disabling it removes the attack vector and is a mitigation for all three vulnerabilities.

bullets.text: Cisco PSIRT reports no known public announcements or malicious use.
bullets.quote: The Cisco Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is not aware of any public announcements or malicious use of the vulnerabilities that are described in this advisory.

details.text: Multiple vulnerabilities in the Operation, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) feature of Cisco NX-OS Software, known as Next Generation OAM (NGOAM), could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges or cause a denial of service (DoS) condition on an affected device. These vulnerabilities are due to improper input validation of IP traffic when NGOAM is enabled. An attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by sending crafted packets to an IP interface on an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges and could cause process crashes, which could result in a reload of the device and a DoS condition. Note: Feature requirements vary for each vulnerability. For details, see the Vulnerable Products section of this advisory. Cisco has released software updates that address these vulnerabilities. There are no workarounds that address these vulnerabilities. [The supplied excerpt ends before the remaining explanation.]

details.text: These vulnerabilities affect Cisco Nexus 3000 Series Switches and Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches in standalone NX-OS mode if NGOAM is enabled and specific features are configured, as detailed in the following list: CVE-2026-76485: To be affected by this vulnerability, the switch must have NGOAM enabled. That is the only requirement. CVE-2026-76486: To be affected by this vulnerability, the switch must have NGOAM enabled and either Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) or Network Virtualization (NV) Overlay enabled. NV Overlay also requires a VXLAN Ethernet VPN (EVPN) VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI) mapped to a Network Virtualization Endpoint (NVE) interface with at least one peer VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint (VTEP) learned (for example, BGP EVPN or an ingress-replication static peer). CVE-2026-76501: To be affected by this vulnerability, the switch must have both NGOAM and SRv6 enabled. Note: Cisco Nexus 3000 Series switches do not support SRv6, and only a subset of Cisco Nexus 9000 Series switches support SRv6. For more information, see Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS SRv6 Configuration Guide, Release 10.6(x) . Determine the Status of NGOAM To determine whether a device is configured with NGOAM enabled, use the show feature | include ngoam command at the Cisco NX-OS CLI. The following example shows NGOAM enabled on a device that is running Cisco NX-OS Software: switch# show feature | include ngoam ngoam 1 enabled Determine the Status of NV Overlay To determine whether a device is configured with NV Overlay enabled, use the show feature | include nve command at the Cisco NX-OS CLI. The following example shows NV Overlay enabled on a device that is running Cisco NX-OS Software: switch# show feature | include nve nve 1 disabled switch# configure switch(config)# feature nv overlay switch(config)# show feature | include nve nve 1 enabled Determine the Status of the NV Overlay VXLAN [The supplied source section is truncated; remaining details are not inferred.]

details.text: Cisco considers any workarounds and mitigations (if applicable) to be temporary solutions until an upgrade to a fixed software release is available. To remediate these vulnerabilities and avoid future exposure as described in this advisory, Cisco strongly recommends that customers upgrade to the fixed software indicated in this advisory. Cisco NX-OS Software To help customers determine their exposure to vulnerabilities in Cisco NX-OS Software, Cisco provides the Cisco Software Checker . This tool identifies any Cisco security advisories that impact a specific software release and the earliest release that fixes the vulnerabilities that are described in each advisory (“First Fixed”). If applicable, the tool also returns the earliest release that fixes all the vulnerabilities described in all the advisories that the Software Checker identifies (“Combined First Fixed”). To use the tool, go to the Cisco Software Checker page and follow the instructions. Alternatively, use the following form to search for vulnerabilities that affect a specific software release. To use the form, follow these steps: Choose which advisories the tool will search-only this advisory, only advisories with a Critical or High Security Impact Rating (SIR) , or all advisories. Choose the appropriate software. Choose the appropriate platform. Enter a release number-for example, 10.4(4) for Cisco Nexus 3000 Series Switches or 16.0(8e) for Cisco NX-OS Software in ACI mode. Click Check .

details.text: There are no workarounds that address these vulnerabilities. If the NGOAM feature is not required, disabling it removes the attack vector and is a mitigation for all three vulnerabilities. Disable the NGOAM by using the Cisco NX-OS CLI command no feature ngoam in global configuration mode on a Cisco Nexus 3000 Series or 9000 Series Switch. While this mitigation has been deployed and was proven successful in a test environment, customers should determine the applicability and effectiveness in their own environment and under their own use conditions. Customers should be aware that any workaround or mitigation that is implemented may negatively impact the functionality or performance of their network based on intrinsic customer deployment scenarios and limitations. Customers should not deploy any workarounds or mitigations before first evaluating the applicability to their own environment and any impact to such environment. Live Protect Shields Cisco has released Live Protect shields for CVE-2026-76485, CVE-2026-76486, and CVE-2026-76501 to temporarily mitigate these vulnerabilities for Cisco NX-OS Software. For information about Live Protect for Cisco NX-OS Software, see Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS Security Configuration Guide . Note: Live Protect shields are temporary mitigations to bridge the gap until software updates can be scheduled. To remediate this vulnerability, upgrade to a fixed software release as noted in the Fixed Software section of this advisory.

To remediate this vulnerability, upgrade to a fixed software release as noted in the Fixed Software section of this advisory.

I spent about 15 years as a consultant working across many well-known consultancy firms and eventually moved to Cisco where I spent time doing security operations center (SOC) design and assessments as well as segmentation before moving to the Talos IR team. I spent many years there, first as an Incident Commander and then a manager of our excellent team of global IR consultants and investigators. stories.title: SonicWall SMA1000: reported exploitation requires careful attribution

bullets.text: BleepingComputer reports exploitation of CVE-2026-102255 in SMA1000 appliances.
bullets.quote: Attackers are exploiting a maximum-severity vulnerability in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances (CVE-2026-102255) that was patched on Tuesday, three days ago.

bullets.text: The named models are SMA1000 6210, 7210, and 8200v; the excerpt excludes SMA100 and firewall SSL-VPN.
bullets.quote: Tracked as CVE-2026-102255 , the flaw affects the Appliance WorkPlace interface on SMA1000 6210, 7210, and 8200v models, but does not affect the SMA 100 Series product line or SSL-VPN running on SonicWall firewalls.

bullets.text: A researcher reports honeypot attempts consistent with the flaw; vendor confirmation differs.
bullets.quote: While SonicWall has not yet flagged this vulnerability as actively exploited in its Tuesday advisory, Previdian founder and security researcher Ryan Dewhurst told BleepingComputer on Friday that the company's honeypot network has detected exploitation attempts consistent with the CVE-2026-102255 flaw.
